asks: Asks the commission to account for rapid growth in south Calgary (Calgary-Shaw) and to narrow population disparities between ridings.

note: Lesser Slave Lake (about 28,000) cited only as an example of population disparity with Calgary-South East (rule 6).

asks: Asks that Calgary-Shaw stay as it is, or if changed, not be combined with rural areas.
Asks the commission to avoid gerrymandering and to keep urban and rural districts separate to protect electoral parity.
Asks that Ogden (Millican Ogden) remain in Calgary-Peigan with its current neighbouring communities.
Asks the commission to avoid partisan gerrymandering and to keep lower-income pockets of Calgary together rather than splitting them.
Asks that Brooks-Medicine Hat stay unchanged, keeping the County of Newell with Brooks and part of Medicine Hat.

note: Says Strathmore and Chestermere populations are 'getting to the point now where that might be one riding all by itself', offered as a reason not to rejoin Brooks with Strathmore; not a request about Chestermere (rule 17).
Lethbridge named only as the south end of the growth corridor to Edmonton; no stance.

asks: Asks the commission to favour blended urban-rural ridings in general and to keep Brooks-Medicine Hat as it is.

note: Red Deer appears in a telecom anecdote about the dense Red Deer perimeter and as a service magnet for Castor; general pro-blend argument (HYBRID-GENERAL G-PRO) names no arrangement for Red Deer.
Mentions the commission's effort to understand Lethbridge growth; buffering-with-rural suggestion is aimed at Calgary and Edmonton perimeters, not Lethbridge.

asks: Asks that Carseland stay with Strathmore, Langdon stay with Chestermere and Strathmore, and Conrich move into a Calgary district.

quote: Keeping Langdon with Chestermere and Strathmore in the same constituency ensures unified representation.
note: Chestermere-Strathmore resident; wants Chestermere kept with Strathmore, Langdon and Carseland. Also asks that Conrich (Rocky View County, not the City of Chestermere) go to a Calgary district; she asks for no part of Chestermere itself to join Calgary. Record tail interleaves Mr. Doerksen's words, not coded here.

asks: Asks that Brooks-Medicine Hat stay as it is and that the County of Newell be kept whole in one district.

Asks that Medicine Hat be separated from its outlying areas, with the city split in half along Highway 120, 13th Avenue, Highway 1, Gershaw Drive and Division Avenue, and Highway 523 used as a boundary.

Asks for two southeast districts: an urban Medicine Hat-North (city north of Highway 1) and Medicine Hat-Cypress-Forty Mile (south Medicine Hat with Cypress and Forty Mile counties), separating Brooks from Medicine Hat.
Asks the commission to note in its report that the Legislature chamber cannot safely hold more seats and to take account of rapid growth and immigration.

note: Lethbridge named only as the site of a prisoner-of-war camp in his book; no stance on districts.

asks: Asks that Medicine Hat no longer be paired with Brooks, endorsing Mr. Wanner's two-district proposal, and agrees the South Saskatchewan River is a sensible dividing line for the city.

Asks that Brooks-Medicine Hat be replaced by an urban Medicine Hat district (north of Highway 1, or the pre-2017 split), with the rest of the city joined to Cypress and Forty Mile counties and Brooks with its own neighbours.

note: Lethbridge named only as a source of river water reaching Medicine Hat; no stance. Record tail after the 10:38 break is Mr. Sakamoto's presentation, not coded here.
Red Deer listed only among faster-growing communities; no stance.

asks: Asks that Brooks and Medicine Hat be separated and that the Medicine Hat boundary follow a natural feature (the river or Seven Persons Creek) rather than streets.
Asks for a Medicine Hat-Cypress district on the south side, with a new district to be worked out for the north.
